newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices slip on growing supply.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices slip on growing supply.

text.p: Most Canadian spot natural gas prices eased on Wednesday as more volumes entered the Alberta market, traders said.
Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was discussed at C$1.37 per gigajoule, down 4-5 cents from Tuesday and flat with with last week. August AECO was quoted at C$1.435.
A Calgary-based trader said NOVA Corp on Tuesday added about 400 million cubic of gas to linepack on its intra-Alberta pipeline network and field receipts continued to rise.
Also, Westcoast Energy Inc was said to have been in the Alberta market during a minor outage earlier in the week at its McMahon, British Columbia plant buying about 300 million cubic feet a day.
The purchases ended on Wednesday, cutting the extra demand, the trader said, adding he expected prices to soften further over the weekend.
Prices also softened in the B.C. market, with Sumas gas quoted in the US$1.04/1.08 per million British thermal units range, down from US$1.10 on Tuesday and US$1.19 last week.
Marketing sources said a cut in transport capacity on Northwest Pipeline was backing gas up into B.C.
In the east, prices at Niagara and Dawn in southern Ontario climbed into the US$2.30/2.32 per mmBtu range, up about 3 cents on the day.
A trader for a large Calgary-based marketing company said the rise coincided with a similar increase in the NYMEX August contract on Wednesday. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
